name: Split Miner
author: István Koren
description: Augusto, Conforti, Dumas, La Rosa and Polyvyanyy's Split Miner: an event log to a BPMN model in five steps — directly-follows graph and loops, concurrency, filtering, split gateways, join gateways. It is not restricted to block-structured models the way the Inductive Miner is, and it is guaranteed to produce deadlock-free ones, which is what makes it the accuracy-versus-simplicity benchmark other miners are measured against. The 2.0 variant reads concurrency from activities whose executions overlap in time rather than from interleaving, and can tell an inclusive choice from a parallel one.

actions.label: Split Miner
actions.description: Discovers a BPMN process model from a traditional event log. Concurrency is detected and pruned out of the directly-follows graph before any filtering, so causality and concurrency are never confused; the filter keeps every activity connected to its most frequent predecessor and successor whatever the threshold does, so no activity is stranded; and split and join gateways are then derived from the concurrency relations rather than guessed from arc counts.

eta.title: Filter percentile (η)
eta.description: How much of the directly-follows graph to keep. Lower keeps more arcs — higher fitness, lower precision, a busier diagram. Every activity keeps its most frequent way in and way out whatever this is set to, so raising it simplifies the model rather than breaking it apart.

variant.title: Variant
variant.description: Which paper's concurrency oracle to use. Split Miner 2.0 needs a log that records when activities start as well as when they finish; on a log without that it has nothing to measure and says so.

epsilon.title: Parallelism threshold (ε)
epsilon.description: How unbalanced two activities' orderings may be and still count as concurrent. 0 demands they be observed in both orders exactly equally often; 1 accepts any pair seen in both orders at all. The value the paper's own tuning across twelve real-life logs settled on is 0.1.

overlap.title: Overlap threshold (ε)
overlap.description: The share of two activities' executions that must overlap in time before they count as concurrent. 1 demands every execution overlap — the strict notion of simultaneousness, which real logs rarely satisfy; lower accepts the parametrised weak form.

maxActivities.title: Activity limit
maxActivities.description: Keeps only the most frequent activities. Split discovery is quartic in the number of activities, so a log with hundreds is worth bounding before it is worth waiting for.

authors.name: István Koren
